name: Aborted Cherubs
classification: Discarded Developmental Specimen / Stunted Cognitive Survivor
origin_lab: Unknown and plural. The Aborted Cherubs are not the product of a single program — they are the product of waste. Every lab that works with human developmental substrate produces failures: developmental arrests, malformed tissue cultures, embryonic and fetal specimens that did not reach specification and were logged as disposed of. The disposal protocols vary by lab. Some incinerate. Some use biowaste processing. Some, in the lower-tier facilities where the oversight is thinner and the disposal budget is smaller, simply discard into the building's drainage infrastructure. The drainage infrastructure connects to everything below. The Aborted Cherubs are what happened when the discards did not die.
origin_method: No single method — accumulated across decades of lab waste from developmental research, geneware trials, embryonic substrate experiments, and failed augmentation studies conducted on pre-natal material. What they share is the point of origin: the drain. Individually, each was disposed of as a failure. Collectively, over time, enough of them survived the drainage system to find each other in the lower levels, and survival in groups proved easier than survival alone, and the intelligence required to survive in a group is a bootstrap — it compounds.
substrate: Human developmental substrate, arrested at varying stages. Not infants — the term is a misnomer born from their size and the softness of their features, which retain the proportional characteristics of very early human development: large head relative to body, wide-spaced eyes, rounded limbs, smooth skin. They are small. The largest documented individual stood approximately 60 centimeters. Their internal biology varies by origin — some have functional organ systems, some have partial or vestigial structures, some have augmentation remnants from the trials they were discarded from. None have functional reproductive organs. None have ever been observed to reproduce. The individuals documented over more than two decades of sightings are, in all likelihood, the same individuals growing no older and no larger, because they cannot.
physical_description:
Small, pale, and disturbingly smooth. The features are human but softened and compressed — the face has the rounded quality of early fetal development, the eyes proportionally large and dark, the nose and mouth reduced. They have hair, fine and light-colored, which grows slowly and hangs around faces that wear no expression that a human observer is able to reliably interpret. They are naked universally — clothing is not something they have acquired or sought — and the paleness of their skin means they carry marks visibly: the scars of old injuries, the bruised shadows of accumulated impacts, and, on many, the visible traces of the procedures that produced them: small incision lines, suture tracks, the circular indentations of probe sites, the ghost of whatever the lab was trying to do before it gave up and put them in the drain.

In the dark of the lower levels, by the light of maintenance strips and bioluminescent seep, they are very easy to mistake for something else entirely — a discarded doll, a bundle of waste material, a trick of light on standing water. Until they move. Their movement is wrong in a specific way: too deliberate for something their size, too quiet, with the particular economy of motion of something that has learned that being seen is never neutral.
behavioral_profile: Scavengers with enough intelligence to be strategic about it. They know their environment in detail — the drainage maps, the maintenance schedules, the places where food waste accumulates and the times at which it does. They communicate with each other through a system that field researchers have characterized as somewhere between gesture and vocalization: soft, wet sounds produced with the mouth that carry further than they should in the resonant pipe systems of the lower levels, combined with touch-based signals when in close proximity. They avoid humans with near-total consistency. The exceptions are documented: they have been observed watching from drain openings and ceiling access points, the dark eyes reflecting light, for periods of up to twenty minutes before withdrawing. They watch people the way something watches that is trying to understand what people are. They have been doing this for over twenty years and they have not yet approached. They have not yet decided if approach is safe. Given what happened the last time they were near humans who had decision-making power over them, this is not an unreasonable position.
threat_level: Negligible. There is no documented case of an Aborted Cherub initiating contact with a human, let alone causing harm. The threat assessment exists only because their presence in the drainage and lower-level infrastructure means that maintenance workers occasionally encounter them, and the encounter is reliably terrifying for the worker and presumably for the Cherub, and in the panic of encounter either party could cause accidental harm. The Cherubs, in documented encounters, retreat. They have never been seen to attack.
containment_status: Uncontained, and the question of whether containment is the appropriate framework is one that the handful of people who know about them in any serious way have been quietly not asking officially for a long time. They are in the drainage systems. They have been in the drainage systems for over two decades. They are not coming up. They are not causing harm. The alternative to leaving them where they are involves finding them, which requires extensive lower-level operations, and then deciding what to do with them, which is a question that nobody with the authority to answer it wants written down anywhere.
known_locations: Primary drainage network, sub-levels 20 through 40, particularly junction points with thermal runoff from adjacent facilities
The abandoned lower maintenance level beneath the old hospital district — several nesting sites documented
Drainage approaches to the Undermarket lower loading, where food waste enters the system at predictable intervals
At least two maintenance workers in the deep infrastructure have reported leaving food near drain access points and finding it taken
contamination_risk: Minimal. They are biologically human in substrate and carry the same pathogen exposure as any individual living in the lower drainage systems, which is not trivial but is not exotic. The deeper concern is the augmentation remnants some of them carry — partial geneware expressions, incomplete cybernetic integrations from the trials they were discarded from — whose long-term biological stability is not known. There have been no documented transmission events of any kind.
pacification_protocol: DPS Directive: None formally issued. The Aborted Cherubs do not appear in any official DPS threat registry because no official entity has formally acknowledged their existence. The informal understanding among the maintenance and infrastructure workers who are aware of them is: do not approach, do not corner, do not report through official channels unless something changes. The pragmatic reason is that an official report creates an official response, and an official response means someone has to write down what they are, and writing down what they are means confronting the question of how they came to exist and what their legal status is, and that question connects to a very large number of labs and a very large number of disposal records and nobody wants to be the person who pulled that thread.
pitiable_qualities: They are the definition of the word. They are what the labs produced and did not want and could not be bothered to ensure were dead. They are the accumulated discard of twenty years of developmental research conducted without the premise that the material being discarded was worth a second thought. They are small and pale and they live in drains and they eat whatever the city's waste provides and they have built, in the dark and without tools and without anyone's help, a life that has lasted over two decades. They watch the people above them through the gaps in the infrastructure. They have been watching for longer than some of those people have been alive. They have not come up. They understand, at whatever depth their intelligence reaches, that up is where the decision was made to put them in the drain, and that nothing about the world above has changed in a way that makes up safer than where they are.
story_hooks: A maintenance worker has been leaving food at a specific drain access for eight months. Recently, something has been left in return — small objects, neatly arranged: a fragment of glass worn smooth by water, three identical bolts, a piece of wire bent into a shape that might be deliberate. The worker is not sure what to do with this.

A runner pursuing a target into the deep drainage encounters a group of Aborted Cherubs in a junction space. The Cherubs freeze. The runner freezes. The target, not having noticed, keeps moving. The runner has approximately fifteen seconds to decide whether the Cherubs are in danger from the target or the target is in danger from them, and the answer to that question may say something about what happens next.

A researcher tracing the disposal records of a recently shut-down lab realizes that the disposal logs for developmental waste going back eighteen years don't add up — the volumes logged as incinerated are smaller than the volumes produced. Someone has known about this for a long time and has been quietly ensuring the discrepancy was never reviewed. That someone still works in the building.
